title: Juniper and the Archive
premise: Mara Fairweather, caretaker of the abandoned Svalbard-2 seed vault, has spent two decades as a neutral cargo hauler in a system split between the Earthborn fleet and the Martian Concord. When gravity fails for nine seconds system-wide, Mara learns it was a signal from the Archive itself—an ancient orbital library his mother helped build, which has chosen him as its inheritor. The Archive holds the cryosleep keys to half of humanity's frozen colonists, and both factions will kill to control them. As the fleet's truce collapses, Mara must decide which half wakes: the militarized Earthborn who could win the war, or the Concord's scientists who could end it. In the end, Mara splits the keys, waking one ship from each side and forcing the survivors to share the Archive—or lose everything.
about_author: Lena Crane is the pen name of a former logistics analyst who spent six years writing technical manuals for orbital freight companies before turning to fiction. She lives in a coastal town where she keeps an actual seed collection and writes at dawn.

chapters.title: Nine Seconds of Falling
chapters.summary: POV Mara. Hauling cargo through contested orbits, Mara feels gravity die for exactly nine seconds—everywhere in the system. His cargo floats, his coffee hangs, and when weight returns he finds a coordinates packet embedded in his ship's firmware that shouldn't exist. Beat: unease; the invisible man has been seen.

chapters.title: The Caretaker's Ledger
chapters.summary: POV Mara. At the derelict seed vault, Mara reviews twenty years of quiet maintenance logs and realizes the anomaly originated from the vault's deep archive—a level sealed since his mother's death. He finds her handwriting on a maintenance order dated three days before the flicker. Beat: grief resurfacing.

chapters.title: Both Flags Call
chapters.summary: POV Mara. An Earthborn corvette and a Concord skiff arrive simultaneously, each claiming the nine-second event was their weapon test. Mara plays neutral broker, lying smoothly, but both captains note his registry links to the Fairweather name. Beat: the mask slipping.

chapters.title: What Mother Built
chapters.summary: POV Mara. Descending into the sealed archive level, Mara finds a living server garden grown from seed-stock biocomputers—and a recorded message: 'If you're watching this, the system chose you.' The Archive explains it triggered the flicker to locate its heir. Beat: awe curdling into dread.

chapters.title: The Frozen Half
chapters.summary: POV Ilsa Voss, Concord science officer. Aboard the Concord flagship, Ilsa decrypts intercepted data proving the Archive holds cryosleep revocation keys for 400,000 sleepers—half from each faction. Her superiors order retrieval at any cost. Beat: cold ambition; she begins to question it.

chapters.title: Truce Expiry
chapters.summary: POV Mara. The fleet-wide truce formally expires; patrol skirmishes flare across the belt. Mara's old smuggling contacts warn him every faction now has his flight plan. He must move the Archive's core or lose it. Beat: hunted.

chapters.title: Cargo Run to Nowhere
chapters.summary: POV Mara. Mara stages a decoy shipment while physically hauling the Archive's seed-core inside grain containers. A Concord boarding party nearly finds it; Ilsa Voss personally waves him through—for reasons she doesn't yet understand herself. Beat: narrow escape, first spark of alliance.

chapters.title: The Price of Neutrality
chapters.summary: POV Mara. Flashback chapter: how young Mara watched his mother refuse both sides access to the Archive, and how her refusal got her spaced as an 'accident.' His invisibility was survival; inheritance is a death sentence. Beat: understanding his own cowardice.

chapters.title: Ilsa's Arithmetic
chapters.summary: POV Ilsa. Ordered to seduce or coerce Mara's cooperation, Ilsa instead audits the sleeper manifests and discovers her own brother among the frozen Concord colonists—listed as expendable by her own command. Beat: loyalty cracking.

chapters.title: Docking at Ashfall
chapters.summary: POV Mara. Mara hides the core at Ashfall Station, a lawless refinery habitat run by his estranged sister Odile, who sold information to the Earthborn years ago. Their reunion is knives-out; she wants payment for silence. Beat: family as liability.

chapters.title: The Fleet's Offer
chapters.summary: POV Mara. Admiral Reyes of the Earthborn fleet offers Mara citizenship, protection, and his mother's cleared name—in exchange for waking only the Earthborn sleepers. It's everything he's wanted, gift-wrapped in corruption. Beat: temptation made flesh.

chapters.title: Gravity Lessons
chapters.summary: POV Ilsa. Ilsa defects with proof of the Concord's expendable-lists and reaches Ashfall, forcing Mara to choose: turn her over to Reyes as a peace offering, or shelter her and burn his last bridges. He shelters her. Beat: commitment.

chapters.title: Odile's Betrayal
chapters.summary: POV Mara. Odile sells the core's location to Reyes anyway—not for money, but because she believes one woken half is better than a war over both. Earthborn marines seize Ashfall; Mara and Ilsa escape on a burning tug. Beat: loss and rage.

chapters.title: The Archive Speaks
chapters.summary: POV Mara. With the physical core gone, Mara returns to the vault and learns the truth: the seed-core was a decoy his mother built. The real Archive is distributed across the system—it caused the nine-second flicker deliberately, testing whether anyone would share rather than seize. Beat: revelation; the trap was always ethical.

chapters.title: Countdown at Ceres
chapters.summary: POV Ilsa. Both fleets converge on Ceres, where the Archive's master node orbits. Reyes plans to crack it by force; the Concord plans the same. Ilsa broadcasts the expendable-lists to both fleets' crews, sowing mutiny in the ranks. Beat: chaos as leverage.

chapters.title: Boarding the Node
chapters.summary: POV Mara. Amid the Battle of Ceres, Mara docks with the master node using his mother's biometric key. Inside, the Archive offers him full control: choose which half wakes, and it will enforce the choice absolutely. Absolute power, offered politely. Beat: the thematic crux.

chapters.title: Which Half
chapters.summary: POV Mara. Alone in the node, Mara walks the memory-gardens of the sleepers—Earthborn soldiers and Concord scientists, children on both lists. He drafts orders splitting the keys, then hesitates, knowing any split could reignite the war. Beat: paralysis at the summit of power.

chapters.title: Reyes at the Airlock
chapters.summary: POV Mara. Reyes boards the node, wounded, and makes his final argument: mercy now means slaughter later. Mara refuses; they fight in zero-g among the seed racks. Mara wins but cannot execute him—he seals him aboard a drifting shuttle instead. Beat: power declined.

chapters.title: The Split Decision
chapters.summary: POV Mara and Ilsa alternating. Together they wake one ship from each faction—the Earthborn hospital vessel Meridian and the Concord research ship Halcyon—chosen precisely because neither can fight. The Archive enforces the truce around them with gravitational shows of force. Beat: resolution through constraint, not virtue.

chapters.title: Two Ships, One Harbor
chapters.summary: POV Ilsa. The Meridian and Halcyon dock together at the vault. Woken crew from both sides, stripped of weapons and hierarchy, must cooperate to survive the vault's failing systems. First brawls, then barter, then shared meals. Beat: cautious hope earned the hard way.

chapters.title: Inheritance
chapters.summary: POV Mara. Mara formalizes the Archive's charter: keys rotate annually between elected stewards from each faction, and no single hand may ever hold them all. He visits his mother's memorial rack and finally reads her last log entry aloud. Beat: reconciliation with legacy.

chapters.title: Juniper, Blooming
chapters.summary: POV Mara. Months later, the first juniper sprout grown from the vault's original seeds is planted aboard the joint station. Gravity holds steady everywhere. Mara takes a cargo contract again—but this time, everyone knows exactly who he is, and he lets them. Beat: visibility embraced; quiet, hard-won peace.
